CITY
OF SUBULUSSALAM
REGARDING
WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Qanun, what is meant by:
1. City is the City of Subulussalam.
2. City Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Subulussalam.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the regional head and DPRK in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the City of Subulussalam hereinafter referred to as the City Revenue and Expenditure Budget abbreviated as APBK is the annual financial plan of the City Government which is discussed and approved jointly by the Mayor and DPRK and established by Qanun.
6. Medium-Term Development Plan of the City hereinafter abbreviated as RPJMK is a planning document for a period of 5 (five) years.
7. Women are adult humans of female sex and persons recognized by law as women.
8. Women with disabilities are persons who have not been able to accommodate with their surrounding environment due to having disorders, activity limitations resulting in participation restrictions.
9. Women's rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are human rights.
10. Empowerment is an effort to increase the ability of women to obtain access and control over all resources in all aspects of life.
11. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and guarantees for women's rights in all aspects of life.
12. Victims are women who experience threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or become objects of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all forms and aspects.
13. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
14. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or other fields by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and / or community organizations.
16. Community Participation is the involvement of the community in the process of identifying problems and potentials that exist in the community, selection and decision-making about alternative solutions to address problems, implementation of efforts to overcome problems, involvement in the process of evaluating changes that occur.
17. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral lines up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and / or child.
18. Public sphere is in the area or region of the community or women who play a role outside the home.
19. Services are immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
21. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of regional government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
22. Integrated Service Center hereinafter referred to as PPT is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as Integrated Service Center for Women's and Children's Empowerment, Safe House, Children's Social Protection House, Trauma Center Protection House, Women's Social Protection House, Shelter, etc.
23. UPTD PPA is a technical and integrated service unit in handling women and children victims of violence.

Article 16
(1) The city government is obligated to provide information and access to all forms of protection against actions that harm women.
(2) The forms of protection as referred to in paragraph (1) include the fulfillment of basic rights, security, consultation and legal assistance, psychosocial support, social reintegration and other necessary actions.
(3) The City Government is obligated to provide free legal assistance to women, women with disabilities, women living with HIV/AIDS, poor women, minority women, women victims of violence, women victims of conflict and natural disasters, and indigent women who face legal problems.
(4) Legal assistance as referred to in paragraph (3) must be carried out in accordance with human dignity and worth.

Article 8
The rights of women as referred to in article 7 paragraph (1) include:
a. Women obtain equal rights and obligations in life within marriage and family, both as parents to their children, and as husband-wife partners and there shall be no coercion in marriage.
b. Women obtain the right to education and teaching in all types, levels, and pathways of education, without any obstacles and pressure whatsoever in order to improve their skills and quality of life.
c. Women obtain the right to work and positions in all institutions both governmental and non-governmental institutions and at all levels for the purpose of increasing income and family welfare.
d. Women obtain the right to special protection in the implementation of their work or profession both in the public and domestic spheres against matters that threaten their safety and/or health in relation to reproductive functions.
e. Women obtain access to optimal and quality health information and services.

Article 14
(1) Every service provider institution is obligated to conduct disaggregated data collection on women with disabilities, women with HIV/AIDS, women victims of violence, women victims of conflict and natural disasters who are handled in accordance with the documentation format that has been established.
(2) The case handling mechanism can be through non-litigation and litigation channels.
(3) Non-litigation channel as referred to in paragraph (2) is an effort to resolve cases of violence against women outside the court channel.
(4) Litigation channel as referred to in paragraph (2) is an effort to resolve cases of violence against women using the court channel.

Article 21
• (1) The city government provides adequate employment opportunities based on the level of education and skills possessed by women, women with disabilities, women with HIV/AIDS, minority women, poor women, women victims of violence, and women victims of conflict and natural disasters.
(2) The city government coordinates with agencies/institutions/business entities and employment providers to ensure favoring women in employment opportunities.
(3) Job information and job seeker selection are conducted in an accountable, fair, transparent, and inclusive manner.
(4) The City Government may take temporary special measures by prioritizing women with disabilities, women with HIV/AIDS, minority women, poor women, women victims of violence, and women victims of conflict and natural disasters.
(5) Women as referred to in paragraph (4), in obtaining employment in accordance with their knowledge or skills, by developing policy mechanisms toward private companies and the government as well as State-Owned Enterprises.

Article 15
(1) Non-litigation channels in handling cases of violence against women can be carried out through restorative justice mechanisms and customary justice mechanisms.
(2) Gampong officials and other government officials are obligated to involve women in the process of resolving cases of violence against women through non-litigation.

Article 4
(1) Activities for the empowerment and protection of women are carried out and coordinated by the Regional Work Unit whose scope of duties and responsibilities is in the field of empowerment and protection of women.
(2) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out together with relevant agencies, offices, educational institutions, the business sector, and community organizations related to the empowerment and protection of women.

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION
Section 1
Purpose and Objectives

Article 12
The City is obligated to provide support for the development of service institutions for women with disabilities, women with HIV/Aids, minority women, poor women, women victims of violence, women victims of conflict and natural disasters, whether organized by the government or private sector.
(2) The City Government is obligated to:
a. Establish Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT) and/or Integrated Service Centers (PPT) at Regional General Hospitals, Police Hospitals, and Private Hospitals for the provision of services for women with disabilities, women with HIV/Aids, women victims of violence, and women victims of conflict and natural disasters;
b. Establish Integrated Service Centers for Women and Children Empowerment or UPTD PPA as a Technical Implementation Unit under the City Office of Women Empowerment, Child Protection and Family Planning; and
c. Establish a Shelter and Trauma Center (RPTC) as a facility to provide protection and assist women with disabilities, women with HIV/Aids, women victims of violence, women victims of conflict and natural disasters in psychosocial and traumatic recovery.

CHAPTER VII
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 30
(1) Every member of the community has the right to obtain opportunities to participate in the empowerment and protection of women.
(2) Every member of the community has the right to obtain or provide information on violations of women's rights.
(3) The community has the right to convey suggestions and opinions in efforts to empower and protect women.

CHAPTER II
WOMEN'S RIGHTS
Article 7
(1) Every woman has basic rights as a human being that must be protected, promoted, upheld and fulfilled in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(2) Matters related to reproduction and women’s natural disposition do not prevent a woman from obtaining her rights in the empowerment and protection of women.

Article 6
The empowerment of women is based on two pillars consisting of:
a. Protection
b. Empowerment

Article 20
(1) The City Government is obligated to improve the quality of life of women starting from the kampong, sub-district and city levels. (2) The City Government is obligated to provide equal opportunities to women and men in improving their quality of life proportionally.
(3) The City Government is obligated to endeavor to establish special education and training institutions or productive skills institutions for women as preparation for entering the workforce or creating independent businesses.
(4) The City Government is obligated to ensure the realization of a level of social welfare for women.
(5) The City Government is obligated to provide facilities and infrastructure for the acceleration of improving social welfare for women.
(6) Social welfare as referred to in paragraph (1) is the fulfillment of needs for clothing, food, shelter, education, health, employment and peace/tranquility of the environment.

Article 17
(1) The City Government is responsible for providing a guarantee to accompanying officers to obtain access to information and to provide accompaniment to women victims for the legal process being undertaken.
(2) The guarantee as referred to in paragraph (1) is provided through a Mayor’s Decree issued to the Accompanying Personnel for Women Victims.

Article 22
(1) conducting control, guidance, and supervision of the implementation of the program for the Fulfillment of women's rights.
(2) control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the SKPK responsible for women's affairs.

Part 2
Government Obligations Toward Women

Article 26
(1) The Mayor is responsible for the annual report on the implementation of women's protection.
(2) Reporting on the implementation of women's empowerment and protection is conducted in a tiered manner starting from the kampong level.
(3) The Keuchik submits reports periodically to the Camat every three months.
(4) The Camat submits reports periodically to the Mayor through the Chair of Bappeda every six months.
(5) The Head of City Bappeda submits reports to the Mayor periodically every six months, including therein reporting on the City PUG Working Group.
(6) City BAPPEDA also conducts general evaluations of the implementation of women's empowerment and protection based on the RPJMK and SKPK Renja.
(7) The Mayor submits reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and protection periodically to the Governor of Aceh every year.
(8) Reports are submitted to the Governor of Aceh with copies to the DPRK.
(9) Reports as referred to in paragraph (1) are also copied to the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection and the Minister of Home Affairs.

CHAPTER VI
MONITORING, EVALUATION AND REPORTING
Article 25
(1) The Mayor conducts monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and protection. (2) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.
(3) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out at each SKPK and in a tiered manner between levels of government.
(4) Monitoring and evaluation is conducted before the preparation of programs or activities for the following year. (5) The implementation of monitoring and evaluation is carried out in cooperation with sub-district and kampong governments as well as civil society organizations.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX
OTHER PROVISIONS
Article 33
To accelerate efforts for the empowerment and protection of women, the Government of Subulussalam City is obligated to implement special policies.
